items.title: Tom Lellis interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, July 31, 2007
items.q: there was a great disc jockey in Cleveland, Ohio, where I was born, his name was Bill Randall, and he played all those great singers.

ctx.x: Did you have a musical household when you grew up?

No, but my mother, getting up for breakfast in the morning, there was a great disc jockey in Cleveland, Ohio, where I was born, his name was Bill Randall, and he played all those great singers. And my mother, who came from a kind of blue collar, no frills background, but when the radio is on and a great singer was playing, she would just light up and start dancing around the kitchen and sing harmony with Mel Torme and Ella Fitzgerald. And she would break into harmony, and I would go, “How do you do that?” like…
Did you go through the high school chorus and all of that?
